A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Photo3D and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The retained material can be matched across appendix reorganization and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, human and Gemini assessments, loss ablations, and qualitative experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds dataset-quality measurements, a test-time optimization comparison, and additional qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The dataset-construction pipeline, CLIP perceptual adaptation, DINOv3 semantic matching, and three paradigm-specific training procedures remain unchanged. The alternative image-generator demonstrations do not introduce a new Photo3D algorithm or loss.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Photo3D-MV with 10K objects across 373 categories and evaluation on ImageNet, GSO, OmniObject3D, and DTC. The new analyses concern retained generation tasks and model choices, without establishing additional dataset, domain, or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix B.1 adds a test-time optimization baseline against Photo3D. The illustrated generator comparison changes from GPT-4o-Image, Gemini-2.5-Flash, and Flux.1-Kontext in v1 Figure 8 to GPT-4o-Image, Gemini-3-Pro-Image-Preview, and FLUX.2-dev in v2 Figure 10. Table 1's comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a before-and-after assessment of generated training views using Probe3D consistency and MANIQA, plus a test-time optimization comparison using MUSIQ and runtime. These are additional evaluation procedures; the existing benchmark sample sizes, preprocessing, training budgets, resolutions, and human-evaluation setup remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The supplementary validation substantially broadens the questions tested: whether training outperforms test-time enhancement, whether enhanced realism preserves multi-view consistency, and whether coupled optimization corrects geometry. Generator-choice analysis is also updated. These extend beyond the retained supervision ablations and four-view latent-construction failure analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated training runs, random seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The added measurements use point estimates without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain all numerical results. New appendix measurements report consistency changing from 0.854 to 0.842 and MANIQA from 0.438 to 0.655 after image enhancement. The new baseline comparison reports Photo3D versus test-time optimization at MUSIQ 76.6 versus 71.5 and 10 seconds versus over four minutes. Additional qualitative results concern newer generators and geometry correction.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and objectives in Equations 1–7 are unchanged. The newly used consistency metric is referenced without adding a mathematical definition, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about structure-aligned photorealistic generation, Photo3D-MV, and applicability across 3D generation paradigms. The added analyses do not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the dataset measurements as a favorable realism–consistency tradeoff and attributes test-time optimization failures to geometry mismatches. It also discusses compatibility with newer image generators and explicitly distinguishes geometry correction by coupled Trellis optimization from decoupled methods' dependence on good initial geometry.

D1.justification: Figure 8 newly documents the baseline sequence of Trellis generation, GPT-4o enhancement, and optimization using Ladapt plus Lmatch, with stage timings. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, dataset prompts, color processing, and project access information remain unchanged; detailed optimization settings for the new baseline are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Nano Banana Pro/Gemini-3-Pro-Image-Preview and FLUX.2 to support the newer generator examples. The existing related-work discussion and positioning against prior 3D generation approaches remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short generator-flexibility paragraph in Section 4.1, divides Appendix B into test-time and training-time subsections, introduces generator-choice and geometric-correction sections, and moves More Results from Appendix C to D. Most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4 expands to include original and enhanced views, and Figure 6 changes Real3D's multi-view montages to single rendered views. The appendix replaces the older generator figure and adds optimization and geometry-correction illustrations. The three large result galleries are retained as Figures 12–14, with localized resizing and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful evidence for the choice of training-time enhancement, quantifies the realism–consistency tradeoff, and clarifies geometry limitations. These strengthen support for the unchanged central results. The gain is limited by sparse reporting of the new experiments' sample sizes and settings, while replacing the older generator-comparison figure removes some direct evidence for the original GPT-4o selection rationale.
